mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, higher discount rates applied to future cash flows reduce the present value of expected corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified rate hike episode (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment (PAYEMS) above the prior quarter's average coincides with stronger consumer demand, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds prior quarter average by >10,000 in the current month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with the employment surge (Pearson R < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) grows faster than consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL), it indicates supply-side strength that supports higher future earnings expectations, yielding positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth rate > CPIAUCSL growth rate over the next month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative despite the identified positive signal in the evidence snapshot.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) below 300 over two consecutive months suggests deflationary pressure, which typically precedes equity risk-off flows and negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive or flat during the deflation episode.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4% for three months indicates a labor market softening, which reduces growth expectations and produces negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are positive during the unemployment rise period.

mechanism_narrative: When manufacturing activity (HOUST) exceeds 1,200 (monthly), it signals industrial resilience and supports optimism about future demand, driving positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are flat or negative despite the signal.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) over two months suggests supply-side softness, which can lead to risk aversion and negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for two consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL falls for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive during the identified weakening period.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 4%), the equity discount rate is expected to decline, enhancing expected future cash flows and producing positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: regime: FEDFUNDS < 4% for the current month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically higher than the pre-easing period baseline (p > 0.05).
